questions.q: According to the summary, what are the two main kinds of speech?
a: Nourishing speech and toxic speech
Honest speech and polite speech
Mindful speech and habitual speech
Loving speech and neutral speech
questions.why: Lesson 1 divides communication into nourishing speech, which understands and stays positive, and toxic speech.

questions.q: What did the Buddha do when two people asked him the same question about death?
a: He gave different answers suited to each person's understanding
He refused to answer until they had studied more
He gave exactly the same answer to both of them
He told them to ask someone else instead
questions.why: Lesson 3 uses the story to show that loving speech must fit the person hearing it.

questions.q: What does mindfulness let you do when someone speaks to you harshly?
a: See their words as a sign of their own suffering and take them less personally
Reply with equally sharp words so they understand your limits
Ignore the person completely until they apologize
Report the conversation to someone in authority
questions.why: Lesson 1 says mindfulness helps you judge less and recognize toxic speech as a result of inner suffering.

questions.q: What simple practice does the summary recommend for communicating with yourself?
a: Sitting down and concentrating on your breathing
Writing a daily list of your goals and worries
Talking aloud to yourself in the mirror each morning
Reviewing your conversations before falling asleep
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests taking a minute to sit and focus on breathing, which brings you into the present.

questions.q: What is the first rule of loving speech, according to Hanh?
a: Always tell the truth, but speak it gently
Say only what will make the other person happy
Wait until you are calm before saying anything
Match the other person's tone and vocabulary
questions.why: Lesson 3 says loving speech begins with truthfulness, delivered with gentleness so it builds trust.
